## The scientific model

<!-- What causes what? Draw it before writing any statistics. Which paths does
the estimand need, and which ones would confound it? -->

```{r}
#| label: dag
dag <- dagitty::dagitty("dag {
  Skill -> Makes
  Attempts -> Makes
  Skill -> Attempts
}")
plot(dagitty::graphLayout(dag))
```

## Simulating from the generative model

<!-- Write the scientific model as a simulation. If you can't simulate it, you
don't understand it well enough to estimate it. -->

```{r}
#| label: simulate
sim_season <- function(n_teams = 30, mu = qlogis(0.36), tau = 0.15,
                       mean_attempts = 37 * 15) {
  theta <- rnorm(n_teams, mu, tau)
  attempts <- rpois(n_teams, mean_attempts)
  tibble(
    team = paste0("T", seq_len(n_teams)),
    attempts = attempts,
    makes = rbinom(n_teams, attempts, plogis(theta)),
    p_true = plogis(theta)
  )
}

sim <- sim_season()
```

## The statistical model

<!-- The model in math, then in Stan. Say why each prior is what it is. -->

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{makes}_j &\sim \text{Binomial}(\text{attempts}_j,\ \text{logit}^{-1}(\theta_j)) \\
\theta_j &= \mu + \tau z_j, \quad z_j \sim \text{Normal}(0, 1) \\
\mu &\sim \text{Normal}(-0.5, 0.3) \\
\tau &\sim \text{Exponential}(5)
\end{aligned}
$$

```{r}
#| label: compile
mod <- cmdstan_model("stan/model.stan")
mod$print()

to_stan <- function(d, prior_only = 0) {
  list(N = nrow(d), attempts = d$attempts, makes = d$makes,
       prior_only = prior_only)
}
```

## Prior predictive check

<!-- Do the priors imply plausible basketball before seeing any data? -->

```{r}
#| label: prior-predictive
prior <- mod$sample(to_stan(sim, prior_only = 1), seed = 1,
                    chains = 4, refresh = 0)

prior$draws("p", format = "draws_df") |>
  as_tibble() |>
  select(starts_with("p[")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), values_to = "p") |>
  ggplot(aes(p)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Team three-point % implied by the priors", y = NULL)
```

## Can the model recover what we simulated?

<!-- Fit the simulated data. If the model can't recover known parameters,
it can't be trusted with real ones. -->

```{r}
#| label: recovery
fit_sim <- mod$sample(to_stan(sim), seed = 2, chains = 4, refresh = 0)
check_fit(fit_sim, variables = c("mu", "tau", "p"))

summarise_draws(fit_sim$draws("p"), "mean",
                ~quantile(.x, c(0.05, 0.95))) |>
  bind_cols(sim) |>
  ggplot(aes(p_true, mean)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = `5%`, ymax = `95%`)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "True value (simulated)", y = "Posterior mean and 90% interval")
```

## The data

<!-- Where it came from, what the cutoff is, what you had to clean, and
anything odd. The snapshot is saved in this post's data/ folder the first time
this runs and reused after that. Check column names with glimpse(). -->

```{r}
#| label: data
#| eval: !expr USE_REAL_DATA
team_box <- snapshot(
  "team_box", as_of = AS_OF,
  fetch = function(as_of) {
    hoopR::load_nba_team_box(seasons = hoopR::most_recent_nba_season()) |>
      filter(game_date <= as_of)
  }
)

d <- team_box |>
  group_by(team = team_display_name) |>
  summarise(attempts = sum(three_point_field_goals_attempted),
            makes = sum(three_point_field_goals_made))
glimpse(d)
```

## Fitting the real data

```{r}
#| label: fit
#| eval: !expr USE_REAL_DATA
fit <- mod$sample(to_stan(d), seed = 3, chains = 4, refresh = 0)
check_fit(fit, variables = c("mu", "tau", "p"))
```

## Posterior predictive check

<!-- Does data simulated from the fitted model look like the real data?
Where it doesn't is where the model is wrong. -->

```{r}
#| label: ppc
#| eval: !expr USE_REAL_DATA
ppc_intervals(
  y = d$makes / d$attempts,
  yrep = sweep(fit$draws("makes_rep", format = "draws_matrix"), 2,
               d$attempts, "/")
)
```
